title: Wednesday Quick Tip
subtitle: A short talk between innings
hook: How long is your talk between innings, really?
intro: Your team comes in from the field.
You have six things you want to say.
statement: Kids hold onto one or two points, not six.
q1: Do you keep it to one clear point —
q2: or cover everything while you have them?
q3: What do kids remember from your dugout talks?
t1: There is no perfect answer here. But the next inning starts better
t2: when kids carry one idea back out.
cta: Coaches — how long are your dugout talks?
ctaLines: One point. Water. Check the lineup.
ctaPrompt: Share your dugout habit below. There are no wrong answers.
caption:
How long is your talk between innings, really?
Your team comes in from the field. You have six things you want to say.
Kids hold onto one or two points, not six.
One clear point or cover it all. There is no perfect answer.
How long are your dugout talks? Share your habit in the comments.
